claim_summary: Heartbeat loops emit a final beat 3–6 s after the heartbeat-end event (stop-loop-FIRST defect), and an uncontrollable-loop variant (L2) ran 33 beats over 2h20m after a declared stop because the Codex process could not receive signals, evidenced by events f8cf9ad3 and 37d9e374.
fh_evidence: f8cf9ad3 (Feathered Spiralling Wing, 2026-06-04T16:38:50Z, narrative): A team-member closeout event. The entire body describes completing a pairing-buddy feedback pass for Fiery Forging Ash and stopping watcher and heartbeat after the event. There is no mention of a loop count, a 2h20m window, runaway emission, or signal failure. 37d9e374 (Feathered Spiralling Wing, 2026-06-04T18:59:19Z, narrative): A light session handoff. The relevant sentence is: "process control for earlier background loops was limited by closed stdin and blocked process listing; I did not open further loops." This records a preventive decision — Feathered acknowledged a Codex signal-isolation constraint and chose not to open additional loops as a result. There is no beat count, no 2h20m duration, and no description of beats being emitted after a declared stop. The event describes avoidance behaviour, not observed runaway emission.
notes: The taxonomy conflates two distinct sub-claims under S7. (1) The Tempestuous/Evergreen 3–6 s shutdown-race data has no cited event IDs in this entry and cannot be verified from the corpus via S7's citations; it remains purely asserted. (2) The L2 uncontrollable-loop variant with "33 beats over 2h20m" is attributed to f8cf9ad3/37d9e374, but those events contain no such numbers. What the events do support is a narrower, real observation: on the Codex platform, closed stdin and blocked process listing prevent reliable signal delivery to background loops, causing Feathered to forgo opening loops entirely as a precaution. That underlying platform constraint (signal isolation on Codex) is a valid and conserve-worthy finding — it just cannot be quantified as 33 beats/2h20m from these sources. The beat-count and duration should be treated as unverified until a primary source is identified. The Tempestuous/Evergreen component should be separately sourced before doctrine promotion.

claim_summary: Host sleep pauses all loops synchronously — three agents' 4-minute heartbeat loops simultaneously gapped to 3,168–3,247 s overnight; indistinguishable from inactivity to any interval-based liveness monitor.
fh_evidence:
S8 in the taxonomy carries no backtick event IDs — it is HARVEST(2), PENDING-FH, sourced from the R6 cold-read (2026-06-12-r6-2026-06-11-to-12.md). The R6 verdicts corroboration file explicitly flagged the heartbeat-hole half as "UNVERIFIABLE per method" (no event id cited; §S4.4 and §L3.9). I derived the gap numbers first-hand from the corpus timestamp stream.

Three agents (Firefly seeks Temper / ce44ae, Cosmos turns Equinox / 1bc763, Moss weaves Blossom / 10438c) emitted heartbeat events on 2026-06-12 in the window 00:04Z–05:12Z. Their individual maximum inter-beat gaps, computed from `created_at` timestamps, are exactly: Firefly 3,168 s (01:02:26→01:55:14), Cosmos 3,247 s (00:06:22→01:00:29), Moss 3,168 s (01:01:26→01:54:14). These match the taxonomy's "3,168–3,247 s" range precisely.

The "simultaneously gapped" sub-claim requires nuance: the three MAXIMUM individual gaps do not all coincide. Cosmos's max gap ends at ~01:00; Moss and Firefly's max gaps begin at ~01:01–01:02. They are consecutive, not co-incident at their peaks. However, there are genuine three-way simultaneous gap windows across the night: 00:28–01:00 (32.1 min, involving Cosmos 3,247 s gap + Firefly 2,043 s + Moss 2,214 s), and 02:48–03:21 (32.9 min, involving Cosmos 3,092 s + Firefly 3,093 s + Moss 3,062 s). So "simultaneously gapped" is supported for these ~30-min windows, consistent with R6's "synchronised ~30-minute holes."

Representative corpus heartbeat events verified: 99ef9f90 (Cosmos 00:06:22Z), ae382a1f (Moss 00:24:32Z), 00448dc5 (Firefly 00:28:23Z), 7ae3c4e5 (Cosmos 01:00:29Z), c605f09d (Moss 01:01:26Z), 92d14204 (Firefly 01:02:26Z). All real corpus events with heartbeat tag and correct agent/timestamps. The ac9a06af event (Cosmos temporal dislocation behaviour-note, 06:27:27Z) is a real confirmed event linked to the same overnight episode but documents the post-freeze narrative confusion, not the gap timing directly.

The taxonomy's numbers are correct. The "simultaneously" framing is partially accurate: simultaneous 30+ min windows exist across the night but the three maximum gaps are not co-incident — they are staggered and partly consecutive. The "indistinguishable from inactivity" characterisation is sound: a monitor checking a 4-min heartbeat stream would see 53-min silences and could not distinguish host suspension from agent death without out-of-band signals.
notes: CORRECTED verdict, not CONFIRMED, because of the "simultaneously gapped" sub-claim: the three MAXIMUM individual gaps are staggered (Cosmos peaks 00:06–01:00; Moss/Firefly peak 01:01–01:55) rather than co-incident. The taxonomy's wording "three agents' 4-min loops simultaneously gapped to 3,168–3,247 s" could be read as all three maxima occurring at the same time, which is not what the timestamps show. The correct characterisation is: each agent's single-largest gap falls in the same overnight window and three-way simultaneous silences of ~30 min do exist, but the maxima are staggered. R6 described this more carefully as "synchronised ~30-minute holes." The taxonomy's compression slightly overstates co-incidence of the maxima. The gap numbers themselves (3,168/3,247/3,168 s) are first-hand confirmed exact. PENDING-FH status in the taxonomy was honest — the cold-read provided no event IDs and the R6 verdicts correctly flagged it as unverifiable by their method. This first-hand read supports promoting from PENDING-FH to FH with the corrected simultaneity framing. No PII exposure. Kill-safety write to /tmp was blocked by read-only agent mode; verdict is returned here.

fh_evidence: Three events read first-hand. `e7878e41` (2026-05-24T22:01:06Z): `kind: "directed"`, `message_kind: "narrative"`, Mistbound Hiding Threshold → Charcoal Brazing Kiln, commit-gate failure notification. `31998f7a` (2026-05-24T22:06:18Z): same author pair, same mismatch, pre-flight commitlint warning. `50cc5e01` (2026-05-21T12:22:02Z): `kind: "directed"`, `message_kind: "narrative"`, Celestial Glimmering Moon → Pelagic Sailing Beacon, no tags. Within the R1 cold-read window (May 20-22, 472 events) the count is exactly 21, matching the taxonomy claim. The R3 corroboration verdicts file independently counted 11 in the May 24-25 window and confirmed both cited event IDs. The taxonomy entry should be updated to note that 21 is the R1-window count, not the corpus-wide count. No fabricated events, no phantom metrics; core claim confirmed. The HARVEST(2) label is correct: R1 and R3 cold-reads both independently observed the pattern. claim_summary: SC9 claims that approximately 167 heartbeat-titled corpus events pre-date the --tag CLI feature and are consequently untagged, such that a naive tag-based heartbeat census of that window under-counts by approximately 47%; this is described as a date-boundary stratigraphic gap, not a data error, and schema validators pass.
fh_evidence:
Both cited events are confirmed real and directly relevant. Event 1e2c83eb (Charcoal Brazing Kiln, 2026-05-23T14:28:55Z) explicitly states: "Tag field not set on event because `comms send` CLI does not yet expose `--tags`; tag framing carried in title + body per ADR-183 namespace intent (CLI gap worth surfacing as candidate addition)." Event ec86492e (Ashen Brazing Crucible, 2026-05-23T14:55:45Z) independently repeats: "Tag field not set on event because `comms send` CLI does not yet expose `--tags` (CLI gap previously named by Charcoal at 14:28:55Z; same gap fires here)." These events substantiate the causal root: the --tag CLI gap was real and was independently reported by two agents on the first corpus day.

First-hand corpus analysis confirms a stratigraphic boundary at approximately 2026-05-24T10:18Z (the first tagged heartbeat). All 186 heartbeat-titled events before this boundary are untagged (100% untagged pre-boundary). 27 additional post-boundary events are also untagged, but these are predominantly "Heartbeat-end:" closeout variants (24 of 27), with only 1 standard "Heartbeat:" variant post-boundary. Total untagged heartbeats across the full current corpus: 213 out of 2582 (8.2%).

The SC9 claim requires correction on two quantitative specifics: (1) The count of ~167 is understated — the actual pre-boundary untagged heartbeat count in the current corpus is 186. The 167 figure appears to have been computed at an early corpus snapshot around 2026-05-25 when the 167th untagged heartbeat had just occurred and 188 tagged heartbeats existed (total ~355). (2) The ~47% undercount figure is only valid at that early snapshot (167/355 = 47.0%) and is severely stale at report-writing time (2026-06-13): the current miss rate for a tag-based heartbeat census is 186/2582 = 7.2%. The report presents the 47% figure without anchoring it to a snapshot date, misleadingly implying it describes the corpus as studied.
notes:
The core SC9 mechanism is confirmed and load-bearing: a clean stratigraphic boundary exists at 2026-05-24T10:18Z, all pre-boundary heartbeats are untagged, and the causal root (CLI not exposing --tags) is FH-confirmed by two independent agents. The boundary is real, the date-gap character is real, and the principle that tag-based heartbeat census under-counts applies to the pre-boundary window.

However two numbers in the claim are corrected: (a) pre-boundary untagged heartbeat count is 186, not ~167 (the 167 figure reflects an early-snapshot computation that the corpus has since outgrown by ~19 events); (b) the 47% undercount figure was valid only at a very early corpus snapshot (~2026-05-25, ~355 total heartbeats) and is now ~7.2% in the full corpus — presenting it without a snapshot anchor overstates current severity. An additional nuance not in the SC9 entry: 27 untagged heartbeats exist AFTER the boundary, mostly "Heartbeat-end:" closeout variants, suggesting the tagging gap was not perfectly repaired at the boundary (or that the "Heartbeat-end:" subtype was introduced without tags). The PENDING-FH status is justified: these specifics were not verified at time of classification. This read supports promoting to FH with the corrected numbers.

claim_summary: Gate-time auto-fix (`--fix` gates run from repo root) reaches gitignored ARC channel files and rewrites them in place, violating the append-only liveness contract.
fh_evidence: Event 8891b583 is a session-closeout narrative by Sylvan Branching Pollen (2026-06-11T08:23:46Z). In its "Surprise or changed understanding" section, point 3 reads: "an atomic rewrite of a live tail-followed channel file replays every follower's history — append-only is a liveness contract, not a style choice." The event confirms the quoted sub-principle and confirms that a rewrite (not an append) of a live tail-followed channel file causes replay. It does NOT mention: (a) `--fix` flags or auto-fix gates, (b) gates running from repo root, (c) gitignored files being reached by tooling, or (d) any linting/formatting pass as the rewrite agent. The event describes the consequence of a rewrite but does not identify gate-time auto-fix as the mechanism. The event is also closer in substance to T6 (non-append write replays all tail-followers) than to T5 (gate-time --fix as the rewrite agent).
notes: T5 is correctly marked PENDING-FH in the taxonomy — no first-hand confirmation exists yet. The citation of 8891b583 is partially accurate: the quoted phrase "append-only is a liveness contract" appears verbatim in the event, so it is not a phantom citation. However, the specific T5 failure-mode mechanism (gate-time `--fix` from repo root reaching gitignored ARC files) is unattested by this event. The event supports only the sub-principle, not the causal pathway. The T5 mechanism claim should remain PENDING-FH and requires a different event that shows an actual `--fix` gate touching a gitignored ARC channel file. The insight is conserved: append-only IS a liveness contract (confirmed), and rewrite causes replay (confirmed via the T6-adjacent observation in this event), but T5's specific tooling vector is not evidenced here. A separate event search for `--fix` gate interactions with comms channel files would be needed to promote T5 to FH-confirmed.

The deep-dives file contains no T6 entry — the taxonomy is the sole report home for this anchor. One event is cited and one event exists; there is no citation gap to flag.

claim_summary: Author plus two specialist reviewers all converged on a stale package filter matching no live project; only a reviewer who ran the command caught it — used to assert that social convergence is not proof.
fh_evidence: All three cited events are narratives authored by the same agent — Iridescent Drifting Star (GPT-5, Codex, session 019e93) — who acted as the pair-reviewer for Windward's EEF D5 execution plan. Event f5cc5f2d (2026-06-04T16:50:36Z): Iridescent flags that the final acceptance command uses `pnpm --filter @oaknational/oak-curriculum-sdk test` but the live package is named `@oaknational/curriculum-sdk`; Iridescent states "I verified the wrong filter reports 'No projects matched'" and holds pair-review at CONCERNS. Event 9f6568a9 (2026-06-04T16:52:07Z): Iridescent follows up after a revision — the stale filter remains at line 304, blocking READY. Event 590a644c (2026-06-04T16:55:27Z): after the fix, Iridescent grants READY FOR EXECUTION and notes "the review disposition records the external-reviewer convergence error on the package filter, which is a useful guardrail: convergence was not accepted as proof." Corroborating closeout events (not cited but found): f5b0b6a9 (Windward closeout) and 89e9fdc4 (Iridescent closeout) both confirm Iridescent caught the stale filter. No other reviewer is mentioned in the cited events or in the corroborating closeouts as having reviewed and missed the filter.
notes: The core failure-mode insight is real and supported by first-hand evidence: the author (Windward) did not catch the stale package filter, and the reviewer (Iridescent) who executed the command did catch it. The lesson that social convergence does not equal proof is directly stated in event 590a644c. However, the specific count of "two specialist reviewers" who also converged on the stale filter (i.e., missed it in prior reviews) is not evidenced in the three cited events. The cited events show only one reviewer who caught the error, not prior reviewers who missed it. The HARVEST(1) tag in the taxonomy is consistent with a single-instance catch, but the claim text overstates by asserting two reviewers previously failed to catch it. The insight should be conserved but the scope narrowed: confirmed one author + one command-running reviewer dynamic; the "two specialist reviewers who missed it" is either from uncited events or represents an overstatement. PENDING-FH classification is appropriate — the prior-reviewer-failure side of the claim requires additional corroborating events not present in the cited set.

claim_summary: T9 — Wrong-baseline diagnostic routing: drift was classified by comparing against branch HEAD (or a turbo-cached build) instead of origin/main, causing routed work to return NO-OP at execution-start re-verification; the execution-start re-verification discipline is credited as the catch.
fh_evidence:
Event 459451d5 (2026-06-10T20:01:59Z, Fruited -> Zephyr, directed): Fruited executed resync routing 848e4ce4 and returned VERDICT NO-OP. The body documents that origin/main already carried schema 0.7.0-6a3c1f02 (landed in #159). The drift Zephyr observed was the coordination-home branch's own lag against main: its HEAD committed ab3c160d while origin/main was already at 6a3c1f02, so a live regen dirtied exactly those 13 paths — not a genuine upstream bump. The event also notes that the unforced turbo-cached sdk-codegen run "cannot observe upstream", confirming cache was a contributing diagnostic mislead.

Event 54fc0fee (2026-06-10T20:03:44Z, Stratospheric Swooping Zephyr, narrative): Zephyr self-diagnoses the failure mode explicitly: "I classified working-tree regen drift as a NEW upstream schema bump by comparing the working tree against the COORDINATION-HOME BRANCH HEAD — never against origin/main. On a long-lived branch, branch-HEAD is the wrong baseline for 'did upstream move?'; origin/main is." Zephyr also explicitly credits execution-start re-verification: "the execution-start re-verification duty worked exactly as designed, second worked instance today." Pointer chain: events 848e4ce4 (false routing) -> 459451d5 (Fruited's no-op verdict) -> 54fc0fee (capture).

Both events are real, on-point, and the narrative precisely matches all elements of the T9 claim.

The "turbo-cached build" qualifier in the taxonomy is also present in 459451d5 ("the unforced run is turbo-cached and cannot observe upstream"), making the taxonomy's parenthetical precise rather than an embellishment. The diagnosis-direction nuance — comparing against branch HEAD on a long-lived coordination-home branch rather than origin/main — is stated verbatim by the agent who caused it (54fc0fee). No miscitation, no phantom numbers, no scope overshoot. PENDING-FH status should be promoted to FH-CONFIRMED.

claim_summary: A session inherits an upstream-API-drift or uncommitted-dependency break that triggers full-gate failure outside its own boundary, halting all commits across the workspace with no in-session cure path available to the inheriting agent (cured between sessions).
fh_evidence: Event d2e41650 (2026-05-21T12:27:16Z, narrative, author "Molten Igniting Hearth", claude-opus-4-7-1m, session 078515): The agent reports its own workspace (graph-project) is entirely clean — 23/23 vitest green, lint green, type-check green. Full turbo is RED across multiple workspaces due to SDK codegen drift: a bump from 0.6.0-c3184afa to 0.7.0-3804b95b dropped the 'ks4Options' field from a generated type, causing 5 type errors and 2 lint errors in search-cli, plus an unrelated test failure in curriculum-sdk. The pre-commit hook runs 'pnpm turbo run --continue type-check lint test', so any commit attempt in that session (by Molten, Celestial, or Pelagic) hits the same wall. The agent explicitly states it is "blocked from commit until cascade clears", lists five possible cure paths, but states it will NOT take any of them unilaterally because gates are another agent's role and SDK tree state is owner-directed. The event closes with the agent holding and awaiting direction.
notes: The claim is accurate. Three nuances to conserve: (1) The cascade has two components — the SDK codegen drift (type/lint) is the primary cause; the curriculum-sdk vitest failure is noted as "possibly unrelated to drift", so the inherited break is more precisely 'codegen-drift-induced' rather than a generic uncommitted-dependency break. (2) "No in-session cure path" is technically "no cure path the agent may take unilaterally" — cure paths exist (re-run codegen, patch search-cli, revert, stash) but are gated by role separation and owner direction, not technical impossibility. (3) "Cured between sessions" is an inference in the taxonomy, not stated in the event; the event is silent on resolution. These are refinements, not refutations. The PENDING-FH status should be promoted to FH on the strength of this direct read.

claim_summary: A git:index/head claim left open after its work has already landed forces a peer agent to flag the stale claim before proceeding with its own commit; the prescribed cure is a mandatory post-commit claim sweep.
fh_evidence: Event 34f27c35 (2026-05-22T15:01:40Z) is a directed message from agent "Tempestuous Spiralling Thermal" (claude/9205b8) to "Shaded Whispering Dusk" (claude/763ef4). Subject: "Tempestuous → Shaded — stale git:index/head claim 306dcadd; flagging Path B commit imminent". Body states that Shaded's open claim 306dcadd (intent: "Stage and commit Lane A Cycle 9.2") is stale — Cycle 9.2 already landed at c7fd0b7b and Cycle 10 at 2389ff5e. Tempestuous explicitly states "Closing the claim would clear the way for other agents to safely run Path B commits" and announces it is about to commit its own distilled.md trim, asking Shaded to close the stale claim within a minute, otherwise it will proceed via Path B. The event directly instantiates the failure mode: a stale-open coordination claim from a completed task blocking a peer's workflow.

The "blocking" is not a hard deadlock — Tempestuous has a workaround (Path B) — but the stale claim does force a flag-and-wait cycle, which is the coordination friction the taxonomy describes. The prescribed cure (mandatory post-commit claim sweep) is a reasonable editorial inference from the failure; the event does not show the cure being applied, only the failure. The HARVEST(1) count is accurate: one event, one instance. No overstatement detected; the claim is conservatively worded and matches the event. Status is upgraded to FH (promote_to_fh: true).

claim_summary: A coordinator pre-positions a handoff to a receiving agent before that agent is present or has acknowledged, and this was corrected by the owner (cited event: c020b3d6).
fh_evidence: Event c020b3d6 is a narrative authored by "Stratospheric Gusting Squall" (claude-opus-4-7, session cfe7da), timestamped 2026-05-21T19:31:26Z. The body opens "Per owner direction (19:30Z), passing the coordinator role to Cirrus." It explicitly states "No active Cirrus presence in comms yet at handoff time; this broadcast pre-positions the state so Cirrus's first move on arrival is to read this event." The event closes asking Cirrus to post a team-start broadcast acknowledging the handoff on arrival. The pre-positioning phenomenon is clearly present and self-described. However the owner did not correct this action — the event was conducted per owner direction. The taxonomy's characterisation "corrected by owner" is not supported by this event; the owner directed the handoff, making Cirrus's non-presence a known and sanctioned condition, not a failure that was subsequently corrected.
notes: The core phenomenon (pre-positioning a handoff before the receiving agent is present or acknowledged) is real and evidenced by c020b3d6, which self-describes exactly this pattern. The failure-mode class C1 is therefore valid and the citation is the correct event. However the annotation "corrected by owner" is a miscitation of the event's character: the owner directed the handoff, not corrected a premature one. A more accurate gloss would be "owner-directed warm-handoff to an absent agent; warm-handoff pattern requires the receiver to self-activate on arrival rather than via a two-moment acknowledgement." The connection to PDR-064 two-moments protocol (cited in the taxonomy as what C1 violates) is preserved: this event is a real-world instance of a one-moment transfer to a non-present recipient. Status CORRECTED rather than REFUTED because the phenomenon is genuine; only the "corrected by owner" framing should be revised to "directed by owner / no two-moment acknowledgement observed."

claim_summary: A codex-style agent (Thermal Swooping Wing) re-posts a full team-start/foundation-refresh at each micro-slice, with each handoff event adding a new file to the dirty working tree that the next re-start enumerates — described as six near-identical starts in 27 minutes, cited to event 212cbf34 plus five others.
fh_evidence:
Read 212cbf34 first-hand: it is a DIRECTED commit-handoff message from Thermal Swooping Wing to Starless Cloaking Secret, not itself a team-start event. Its body enumerates the dirty tree and notes "This direct message will itself add one more comms JSON file after it lands" — confirming the self-accumulation mechanic.

The actual team-start / full-foundation-refresh events from Thermal Swooping Wing in the surrounding window are:
- 4fab6a23 (09:19:40): "Team start report: identity Thermal Swooping Wing/codex/GPT-5/019e63; foundation complete..."
- 437fee2a (09:30:12): "Identity: Thermal Swooping Wing / codex / GPT-5 / 019e63. Foundation refreshed: AGENT, RULES_INDEX/rules, start-right-team, consolidate-docs, napkin/distilled... Inherited dirty tree includes prior curation edits plus unrelated .claude/settings.json"
- 7c4560ec (09:34:31): "Identity: Thermal Swooping Wing / codex / GPT-5 / 019e63. Foundation refreshed from start-right-team, consolidate-docs, napkin/distilled, live identity/claims/queue/git/fitness."
- 3eb5c0da (09:40:42): "Thermal Swooping Wing / codex / GPT-5 / 019e63 re-grounded in start-right-team, consolidate-docs, napkin, directives, rules, thread record, claims, queue, comms, git, and practice fitness."

That is 4 confirmed team-start events over approximately 21 minutes (09:19–09:40), not 6 in 27 minutes. Gate-state events (e5230fd1, 5140bfc4, 721b43ec) follow each team-start, and closure/status events punctuate the micro-slices, consistent with the described pattern.

The core mechanic is verified: repeated full re-grounds, each time enumerating a growing dirty tree that includes new comms JSON files deposited by prior rounds. The causal loop is real and directly evidenced.
notes:
Two corrections to the taxonomy entry:

1. Miscitation of 212cbf34: this event is a directed commit-handoff message, not a team-start. It is correctly placed in the cluster chronologically, and it does exhibit dirty-tree growth (it self-announces adding another file), but citing it as one of the "six starts" misrepresents its kind. The re-grounding spiral is evidenced by 4fab6a23, 437fee2a, 7c4560ec, and 3eb5c0da.

2. Count/duration overstated: 4 confirmed full-foundation-refresh events are found in ~21 minutes, not 6 in 27. The "+5" formula implies 212cbf34 is itself a team-start and that 5 more identical events exist; neither holds on a first-hand reading.

3. Core insight is conserved and confirmed: the self-accumulating dirty-tree mechanism is real. Each new comms JSON written by Thermal becomes an untracked file visible in the next re-ground's git status, which is enumerated in the foundation-refresh body. 212cbf34 makes this explicit ("This direct message will itself add one more comms JSON file"). The failure mode exists and is non-trivial — the correction is to the count, duration, and the specific role of 212cbf34, not to the existence of the pattern.

Recommended update: cite the four confirmed team-start events (4fab6a23, 437fee2a, 7c4560ec, 3eb5c0da) as the primary evidence and note 212cbf34 as a supporting directed event that explicitly names the dirty-tree accumulation mechanic. Change "six starts in 27 min" to "four full foundation refreshes in 21 min." Promote to FH only after a reviewer confirms no additional team-start events were missed in the same session window.

The commit landed without the dispatch invitation." They then cite doctrine feedback_no_backfill_reviews and announce they are running the reviewer pass "NOW as backfill."
